A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Platonic Transformer research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, molecular-property prediction, OMol25 energy/force prediction, and runtime experiments, including Fourier-implementation benchmarks in Appendix M.

after.justification: V3 reports original experiments on the retained tasks and additional molecule generation, ProteinMD, ImageNet-1K, and diagnostic analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: The core feature lifting, group weight sharing, and attention/convolution construction remain. Targeted changes include using learned keys with QK normalization for OMol25, extending the architectural description to RoPE on values, and replacing total-energy MSE with per-atom energy MAE in the OMol25 objective (v1 Appendix L.2; v3 Appendix K.2).

E1.justification: V3 adds ImageNet-1K classification, all-atom QM9 molecule generation, and ProteinMD force prediction for backbone and all-atom systems. QM9 regression expands from two reported properties to twelve. These substantially broaden the evaluated populations and task requirements beyond v1's coverage.

E2.justification: The QM9 property comparison replaces FAFormer and G-Hyena with a broader comparator set including DimeNet++, PaiNN, TorchMD-NET, SphereNet, and others, while retaining EquiformerV2. G-Hyena remains in other comparisons. V3 also adds generation comparisons against ADiT, EDM, Symphony, GeoLDM, and ZATOM-1, plus ProteinMD comparators. The OMol25 table replaces the earlier eSEN/MACE presentation with eSEN-sm comparisons.

E3.justification: OMol25 changes from the reported Neutral-split partition, official-test evaluation, and 120-hour budget to 4M training, validation evaluation, and 20/80-epoch comparisons with dynamic batching. V3 retains a conflicting Neutral-split description in Appendix K.1. ScanObjectNN model width, heads, batch size, and epochs change; QM9 adds five-orientation test-time averaging. New generation, diagnostic, and training-runtime experiments introduce further protocols.

E4.justification: V3 adds group-size/head-allocation analysis, learned-key and weight-decay stability tests, measured equivariance errors, an invariant-versus-equivariant attention ablation, attention visualizations, TTA comparisons, and training-step cost breakdowns. The PCA/frame-averaging comparison from v1 is removed. The Fourier implementation analysis is retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V3 adds ± reporting to CIFAR-10 and ScanObjectNN results and reports uncertainty for ProteinMD. Appendix M explicitly describes two-seed stability experiments. Both versions already describe a three-seed hyperparameter sweep and report inference-time variability. V3 does not clearly define the new classification ± quantities or establish increased final-training run counts.

E6.justification: Classification scores and rankings change: ScanObjectNN's best attention entry changes from Flop at 82.0% to Tetrahedron at 86.11%, under revised settings. V3 adds extensive generation, ProteinMD, ImageNet, expanded QM9, and diagnostic results, and replaces OMol25 results under a different protocol. These are not uniformly comparable performance gains. The original QM9 inference timings and Fourier-throughput numbers are retained.

T1.justification: The central equivariance proofs, dynamic-convolution derivation, linear-complexity argument, frequency-steering equivalence, and finite-group Fourier analysis remain substantively unchanged after relocation and renumbering. However, v1 Appendix F's formal frame-equivariance and boundedness definitions, averaging operator, and PCA-frame construction are removed.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain equivariance through geometric weight sharing without changing the standard computation graph, and the dynamic-convolution interpretation. V3's abstract broadens the explicitly claimed competitive applicability to molecular dynamics and molecule generation; it does not substantially redefine the central architectural or theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: V1 presents fixed keys as a crucial regularizer for molecular tasks; v3 replaces this with a qualified expressivity/stability trade-off and permits normalized learned keys on OMol25. V3 also distinguishes molecular validity from stability, discusses capacity versus symmetry resolution, acknowledges target-specific weaknesses on QM9, and explicitly limits guaranteed equivariance to discrete subgroups while noting untested extreme-scale behavior.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands technical documentation with ProteinMD training details, OMol25 dynamic-batch limits, EMA and clipping settings, validation frequency, normalization, and additional architectural controls in Table 12. New runtime measurements specify hardware, software, warmup, and measurement procedures. The front-page code URL remains unchanged; v1's separate reproducibility statement and baseline-access details are removed.

R1.justification: V3 removes the Frame Averaging/FAFormer discussion and associated references, while substantially expanding comparisons and positioning against molecular generators, specialized property predictors, and recent scalable interatomic-potential work. Added references include DiT, EDM, Symphony, ZATOM-1, and PaiNN. The original general motivation relative to equivariant Transformers remains.

P1.justification: Section 3 is reorganized to separate feature lifting and explain the flattened-matrix view of equivariant layers. Existing experimental narratives are extensively rewritten, and QM9 regression and inference timings move into Appendix H. The appendix structure is reorganized, while the related-work stub, frame-averaging appendix, reproducibility statement, and LLM disclosure disappear.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. V3 adds substantial result tables, learning-curve panels, and attention visualizations; expands and restructures QM9 and runtime tables; and redraws Figure 3 with a different token-range axis. The architecture and Fourier diagrams are retained with layout changes and relocation.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens evidence for design arguments that v1 largely asserted: Appendices M–N test key stability, approximate equivariance, and invariant-attention alternatives, while expanded QM9 evaluation and training-cost measurements better establish strengths and limits. These gains improve scientific support beyond merely adding benchmarks. Removing the frame-averaging comparison loses useful evidence, and conflicting OMol25 descriptions and undefined uncertainty notation remain weaknesses, but the diagnostic evidence and more qualified interpretations provide a clear substantial net improvement.
